original_text:
I’ve been learning PySpark and working with Databricks recently. 

I started with the basics, learning how Apache Spark really works :
- What are jobs, stages, and tasks
- How lazy evaluation helps optimize performance
- The difference between transformations and actions

Then I jumped into PySpark hands-on:
- Worked with DataFrames and Spark SQL
- Explored Window Functions, UDFs (User Defined Functions)
- Learned how to handle different file formats like Parquet, Columnar, and Delta
- Understood the difference between managed and external tables in Spark
- And even used display() to build simple dashboards right inside Databricks

To put all this into practice, I chose a real dataset from Netflix and built a Data anlaytics project using Databricks Community Edition.

Here’s what I explored in the project:

Databrick notebook : https://lnkd.in/eRfK_75C

Databricks made it really easy to experiment and visualize everything.
